title: ÆTHER: Friday Night v2 (pop nu-disco with dance hooks)
story: Friday midnight in Bengaluru: a developer shuts her laptop after a brutal release week, rides the empty metro and dances with her friends on a rooftop until sunrise.
script:
# Friday Night: outline (written before the music)

**Genre:** electro disco / nu-disco, built on a funky bassline. 120 BPM, about 96 s, one continuous take.
**Story:** Bengaluru, today. Friday, 11:58 PM. A young app developer shuts her laptop after a brutal release week, rides the empty metro, and walks onto a rooftop where her friends are dancing under string lights. They dance until the sky turns pink.
**Feeling:** relief turning into pure joy. Cool and groovy first, then glittering and huge.
**Raga:** Kharaharapriya in A (A B C D E F# G, the Dorian cousin, which is also the classic funk mode). Hook leans on the warm major sixth F#, with shaken C and G.

| Time | Scene | Music |
|---|---|---|
| 0-4 s | Laptop lid snaps shut. Office lights click off. | The funky bassline ALONE, dry and fat, a slap octave pop on beat one. |
| 4-8 s | She steps into the lift, nodding. | Four-on-the-floor kick and off-beat open hi-hat join the bass. |
| 8-16 s | Lift doors open on the street; she starts walking with a bounce. | Chicken-scratch guitar, clavinet, hand claps on 2 and 4, warm analog pad. |
| 16-28 s | Metro doors slide open; the empty train is all hers. | The hook on a bright analog synth lead with slides; disco string stabs answer. |
| 28-38 s | Her reflection in the window starts dancing. | A soft wordless female voice hums the hook back; Rhodes chords. |
| 38-48 s | She runs up the stairs to the rooftop. | Disco violins do a fast up-run with slides, then strings and synth play the hook together. |
| 48-56 s | Door opens: friends, string lights, the city below. Time slows. | Drums step out to hats and claps; a slap-bass solo break; one bar of just the female voice. |
| 56-72 s | Everyone drags her into the circle. | SLAM back: full groove, the hook on a disco horn section, string counter-melody; wah guitar and synth lead trade the hook, faster. |
| 72-84 s | The whole rooftop dances; confetti from a party popper. | Final chorus: the bassline doubles into sixteenths, voice and strings in unison on the hook. |
| 84-90 s | The first pink light on the skyline. | Whole band plays the hook's last phrase as tight unison stabs, then a stop. |
| 90-96 s | She sits on the ledge, smiling, sunrise. | The bass alone plays the opening line once more, last slap octave A, one string run up. |

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 17:59 on v1: 'give pop touch and some dance hooks'. v2 = the same story, bassline and hook, shaped like a pop song (intro, verse, pre-chorus, big chorus, post-chorus dance hook) with three short catchy dance hooks.

prompt: A brand-new POP nu-disco / electro disco dance hit built around a FUNKY BASSLINE, ONE continuous piece, shaped like a modern chart pop song with big dance hooks. Exactly 120 BPM, A Dorian (A B C D E F-sharp G), four-on-the-floor disco groove with a bouncy, swinging sixteenth feel. The bassline, written out: a fat electric bass playing A with an octave slap pop on the off-beat, ghost-note sixteenths, a walk-up C, D, E into G, then a slide down from E to A; it never stops moving. The main pop hook (the chorus melody), written out: A, A, C, D, slide up to E, lean on F-sharp, E, D, C, D; the answer: G, F-sharp, E, D, C, B, A. Simple, singable, catchy, sung-style with small slides. Three short DANCE HOOKS, each repeated so the listener remembers it: (1) a bright, bouncy synth stab riff of four short notes E, E, G, A on the off-beats; (2) a catchy pitched vocal-chop riff in the post-chorus, a female voice sliced into short melodic 'oh' and 'ah' syllables bouncing A, C, A, E; (3) a funky clavinet and guitar unison lick D, E, G, A answered by a hand clap. Instruments: electric bass, punchy disco drum kit with open hi-hats, snappy hand claps and a tambourine, chicken-scratch funk guitar, clavinet, Rhodes, glossy pop synths, a disco string section, a disco horn section, and a bright female pop voice singing wordless 'ooh', 'oh' and 'la la' melodies (no real words, no shouted chants). 0-4 s: the bassline with the synth stab riff, kick from beat one. 4-16 s (verse): groove with chicken-scratch guitar and claps, the female voice softly sings the verse melody. 16-24 s (pre-chorus): the bass climbs, strings rise, snare builds on every beat, the voice lifts. 24-40 s (CHORUS): the full band, the female voice sings the main pop hook loud and bright, strings and horns answer, the synth stab riff on the off-beats. 40-48 s (post-chorus): the vocal-chop dance hook over the groove, very catchy, bounce and claps. 48-56 s (verse 2): the clavinet and guitar lick trades with the voice, Rhodes chords. 56-62 s (breakdown): drums drop out, only the bass and claps, then one bar of just the voice holding a high note. 62-80 s (final chorus, biggest): everything back, the main hook sung with harmonies, horns and strings in unison, the vocal-chop hook and the synth stab riff stacked together. 80-90 s (outro): the post-chorus dance hook one last time, then the bass alone plays the opening line and ends on a slap octave A with one string run up. Bright, glossy, radio-ready modern pop mix with deep sub bass, the bass and vocals clearly upfront. No side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no filter sweeps, no fade-out. Do not use a rising three-note root-third-fifth call, shouted 'hey' chants, reversed swells, thavil or nadaswaram anywhere.
